lance_optimization.title: Lance Vector Table Optimization
lance_optimization.description: Compact files, prune old versions, improve query performance
lance_optimization.older_than_days_hint: Remove versions older than specified days (recommended: 7-30 days)
lance_optimization.delete_unverified_hint: Aggressive cleanup that may remove in-progress transaction files. Only enable when no active writes.

info.what_answer: Lance uses columnar storage format. Each write creates new files and versions. Optimization compacts small files, prunes old versions, and rebuilds indices to improve query performance and reduce disk usage.
info.why_answer: Frequent small writes generate fragmented files (_transactions, _versions, _deletions), slowing queries and increasing backup time. Regular optimization significantly improves performance.
info.when_answer: Recommended weekly, or immediately after bulk import/delete operations. The app automatically runs light optimization on startup (only removes versions >7 days old).

shell_rules.title: Terminal Command Rules
shell_rules.desc: Manage local terminal commands in one place. Deny rules always win, then Ask, and Allow is evaluated last. Rules use literal matching only; glob and regex patterns are not supported.
shell_rules.default_desc: Keep Ask for most setups and add exceptions only for explicit, repeated commands.
shell_rules.default_allow_warning: Default Allow reduces prompts, but applies only to local calls classified as safe and read-only. Set Allow anyway?
shell_rules.safety_boundary: Allow rules apply only to local, safe, read-only calls. To prevent PATH shadowing and program flags that launch child processes, only trusted shell built-ins or explicit system absolute paths can skip confirmation. Git, rg, dangerous flags, command chains, redirects, interpreters, and external MCP commands still ask. Deny rules always take priority.
shell_rules.help_exact: Matches the complete command and arguments; this is the narrowest scope.
shell_rules.help_prefix: Matches a literal command prefix. Shorter prefixes cover more commands.
shell_rules.help_executable: Matches only the executable identity, without arguments. An Allow rule may cover every subcommand.
shell_rules.note_placeholder: Optional note, such as the use case or rule owner
shell_rules.error_wildcards_not_supported: Patterns such as *, ?, [], and {} are not supported. Enter an explicit literal rule.
shell_rules.error_compound_not_supported: A rule cannot contain pipes, redirects, newlines, or command separators. Split it into one command.
shell_rules.error_executable_only: Executable rules cannot include arguments. Use Exact or Prefix when arguments are required.
shell_rules.error_duplicate: An identical match already exists. Edit the existing rule instead.
shell_rules.broad_allow_warning: This is a broad Allow rule or exposes an interpreter that can run arbitrary scripts. Safety boundaries still apply; confirm the risk before saving.
shell_rules.save_failed: Failed to save terminal command rules
shell_rules.empty_hint: Unmatched commands use the default policy above.
shell_rules.no_matches: No rules match the current filters
shell_rules.preview_hint: This preview explains list matching only. Allow results must still pass backend read-only, safety, and local-execution checks.
shell_rules.bulk_delete_confirm: Delete the {{count}} selected terminal command rules?
shell_rules.relax_confirm: This disables or removes {{count}} Ask/Deny rules and may widen terminal access. Continue?
